title: Kitoko's Current: Electrocution Buildup, Speed Penalty and Build Use in 0.5
summary: Kitoko's Current is a unique Jewelled Gloves in Path of Exile 2 that makes Lightning damage from your Hits contribute to Electrocution Buildup, turning a lightning hit into hard crowd control instead of only Shock. This guide explains what the mod actually does, how Electrocution differs from Shock, the 10-15% reduced Attack and Cast Speed trade-off, which skills build it fastest, why high-damage low-frequency hits are unstable control, and when you should swap back to Rare Gloves.
description: How Kitoko's Current works in PoE2 0.5: Lightning Hits build Electrocution instead of only Shock, the Electrocution vs Shock difference, the 10-15% reduced Attack and Cast Speed penalty and whether increased speed offsets it, best skills for fast buildup, and Rare Glove swap conditions.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 Kitoko's Current unique Jewelled Gloves with lightning electrocution buildup and reduced attack and cast speed

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Kitoko's Current is a unique Jewelled Gloves whose signature line, 'Lightning damage from Hits Contributes to Electrocution Buildup', makes your lightning Hits fill the enemy's Electrocution meter so they get stunned (hard crowd control) instead of only being Shocked for extra damage taken. The cost is a 10-15% reduced Attack and Cast Speed roll that you can only soften, not fully cancel, with increased speed. It drops anywhere in the world and can be created with an Orb of Chance, and you should swap back to Rare Gloves whenever raw speed and damage matter more than locking enemies down.
calloutDetail: Electrocution (control / stun) and Shock (increased damage taken) are two different lightning ailments; Kitoko's Current points your lightning Hits at Electrocution, not Shock.
The speed penalty is 'reduced' (a modifier to your base speed), not 'less' (a multiplier on the final total), so increased-speed bonuses from gear and the passive tree still apply on top of it.
Only lightning damage from Hits counts; Damage over Time such as Ignite or Poison does not build Electrocution, and very high-damage, low-frequency hits are unreliable control on bosses.

answers.label: Use it for
text: Lightning builds that want reliable crowd control: disabling rares and bosses, feeding Combat Frenzy (Frenzy Charges on Electrocute), and stabilising Breach or Delirium farming where packs need to be locked down.

answers.label: Check first
text: Confirm the roll you dropped. A 15% reduced speed roll hurts a caster far more than a 10% roll, and a build that already struggles for cast speed may prefer a Rare Glove with attributes and life or energy shield.

answers.label: Avoid
text: Do not assume it makes every lightning skill better. On bosses with huge life pools the Electrocution threshold is high, and on hit-less or DoT-only setups the gloves do almost nothing.

sections.title: What 'Lightning Hits Contributes to Electrocution Buildup' means
paragraphs: In Path of Exile 2, lightning damage by itself normally only builds Shock, the ailment that makes the target take increased damage. Kitoko's Current changes the rule for your character: lightning damage dealt by your Hits now also contributes to Electrocution Buildup. Electrocution is a separate lightning crowd-control ailment. When an enemy's Electrocution meter fills, the enemy is stunned for a few seconds - it stops acting, which is the same kind of lockdown you get from Freeze, but it comes from lightning and feeds off your Hit damage.

The key phrase is 'from Hits'. Electrocution Buildup scales with the amount of lightning Hit damage you deal, and that damage is measured against the enemy's Elemental Ailment Threshold, which grows with the enemy's maximum life. That threshold is why the same gloves feel amazing on a pack of white mobs (low life, low threshold, fast locks) and awkward on a pinnacle boss (huge life, high threshold, slow locks).

Only lightning damage from Hits counts. Damage over Time - Ignite, Poison, Bleed, or any damage-over-time component - does not contribute to Electrocution Buildup through this glove. A skill that deals its damage as a single massive Hit will build a large chunk of meter at once but may only proc Electrocution rarely; a skill that hits many times for smaller amounts builds the meter steadily and locks enemies far more reliably. That is why high-damage, low-frequency setups are 'unstable control': one big Hit either tops the meter or does not, with little in between.

Kitoko's Current is one of several ways to apply Electrocution. The Electrocute Support Gem redirects one linked skill's lightning damage to Electrocution Buildup instead of Shock, and certain skills such as Shock Nova and Electrocuting Arrow inherently contribute to Electrocution. The glove's advantage is that it is passive and global: every lightning Hit your character lands, from any skill, contributes, with no support-gem socket or specific skill required. The trade you make for that convenience is the reduced Attack and Cast Speed line on the item.
bullets: Electrocution = stun / hard control; Shock = increased damage taken. They are different ailments with different payoffs.
Kitoko's Current points your lightning Hits at Electrocution Buildup, not Shock.
Buildup is mitigated by the enemy's Elemental Ailment Threshold, which scales with the enemy's maximum life.
Only Hits count. Damage over Time does not contribute through this glove.
Faster, smaller Hits build control more reliably than slow, huge Hits.

cells.electrocution: Hard crowd control: the target is stunned and stops acting for a few seconds.
cells.shock: Offence: the target takes increased damage from all sources while Shocked.

cells.electrocution: Only when a source explicitly contributes to Electrocution Buildup - e.g. Kitoko's Current, the Electrocute Support, Shock Nova, Electrocuting Arrow.
cells.shock: Any normal lightning Hit builds Shock by default; no special source required.

cells.electrocution: Yes - lightning Hit damage fills the Electrocution meter, mitigated by the target's Elemental Ailment Threshold.
cells.shock: Yes - lightning Hit damage builds Shock magnitude, also affected by ailment thresholds.

cells.electrocution: High threshold means slow, unreliable locks unless you pour in sustained hit frequency or invest in ailment magnitude.
cells.shock: Still applies reliably; magnitude is what scales, and Shock is easier to maintain on bosses.

cells.electrocution: Enables it globally for all your lightning Hits with no socket cost.
cells.shock: Not this glove's job; Shock keeps working from your other lightning damage as normal.

sections.note: Equip Kitoko's Current when you value locking enemies down more than the Shock damage bonus. The two can coexist - your lightning Hits can still Shock while also building Electrocution.

sections.title: Build usage
intro: Kitoko's Current is a glove for lightning builds that can spare some speed in exchange for lockdown. The builds below get the most from it because they already deal lightning Hit damage frequently and benefit from either stunned enemies or the Frenzy Charges that Combat Frenzy grants on Electrocute.

builds.title: Lightning Spear Amazon
builds.description: The signature synergy. Lightning Spear deals frequent lightning Hits, and Electrocute from Kitoko's Current feeds Combat Frenzy for permanent Frenzy Charges while locking rares. The 10-15% speed loss is the price for that uptime.

builds.title: Ice Shot / Lightning Arrow Deadeye
builds.description: Attack-based lightning scaling with high hit frequency. Lightning Arrow in particular is a classic Electrocute enabler; the glove makes every arrow contribute to control without a support-gem socket.

builds.title: Spark Gemling Legionnaire
builds.description: A mana-stacking caster that fires many small lightning Hits. The cast-speed penalty hurts more here, so a lower (10%) roll or speed investment is advised before committing.

builds.title: Condition: need a Rare Glove's stats
builds.description: If your build is starved for attributes, life, energy shield or resistances, a well-rolled Rare Jewelled Gloves will usually outperform the unique. Swap back whenever control is not the bottleneck.

sections.title: Alternatives: Rare and other Unique gloves
paragraphs: Before locking in Kitoko's Current, compare it against what a Rare Jewelled Gloves and a few other Unique gloves can give you. The unique's only offensive contribution is the Electrocution redirect; everything else it offers (Energy Shield, Dexterity) a Rare can match or beat while also giving you life, resistances and attributes you actually need.

A Rare Jewelled Gloves with high Energy Shield, added attributes, life and a resistance roll will almost always be the better defensive and utility choice once you no longer need the lockdown. Other Unique gloves such as Hand of Wisdom and Action (attribute-scaling attack gloves) or The Burning Man (fire conversion) serve completely different build goals and are not direct competitors for the Electrocution fantasy - they simply show that the glove slot has many stronger raw-stat options.

If you want Electrocution without sacrificing the glove slot, the Electrocute Support Gem gives one linked skill the same redirect at the cost of a support socket, and skills like Shock Nova or Electrocuting Arrow bring it inherently. Those routes free your gloves for defensives while still letting you build Electrocution.
bullets: Rare Jewelled Gloves: better when you need attributes, life, energy shield or resistances more than control.
Electrocute Support Gem: same Electrocution redirect on one skill, no glove slot spent.
Shock Nova / Electrocuting Arrow: inherent Electrocution contribution without any Unique glove.
Other Unique gloves: usually optimise a different stat (attributes, conversion) rather than crowd control.

sections.title: How to get Kitoko's Current
intro: Kitoko's Current is part of the general unique drop pool. There is no boss or quest that targets it, so acquisition is either luck, an Orb of Chance gamble, or a trade.

routes.label: Random world drop
body: It can drop from any enemy in the world once you are at the required level. Higher-tier maps and increased Item Rarity improve your odds of any unique, including this one, but there is no targeted farm.

routes.label: Orb of Chance
body: Using an Orb of Chance on a normal (white) Jewelled Gloves can turn it into a Unique. Several uniques share the Jewelled Gloves base, so this is a low-probability gamble, not a reliable method.

routes.label: Trade with other players
body: Because it is a low-requirement, farmable unique, it is typically cheap on the trade site compared with chase uniques. Buy the roll you want (prefer a 10% speed penalty) rather than gambling.

sections.title: Use, sell or hold
marketNote: Kitoko's Current is a common, low-requirement unique. In the Early Access league its trade price is modest and driven mostly by the speed-penalty roll and the Energy Shield roll. Prices below are indicative snapshots, not live quotes.

use.condition: You run a lightning Hit build that benefits from stun lockdown or Combat Frenzy uptime.
use.first: Equip it and confirm the speed loss is acceptable for your clear feel; prefer a 10% roll.
use.risk: The reduced speed can hurt casters more than attacks; test before committing the slot.
text: Best value in lightning attack or frequent-hit caster builds that want control.
Pairs naturally with Combat Frenzy for Frenzy Charge generation on Electrocute.

sell.condition: You do not run lightning Hits, or you already have a stronger Rare Glove for your stats.
sell.first: List it; a 10% speed-penalty roll sells for more than a 15% roll.
sell.risk: Overpricing a high-penalty roll will leave it unsold; price to the roll.
text: Common unique, so do not expect a premium unless perfectly rolled.
Indicative Early Access trade value is a few Divine Orbs for a low-penalty roll (verify on the trade site for your region and league on 2026-08-03).

hold.condition: You are levelling an alt lightning build or expect to want control in a future character.
hold.first: Stash a 10% roll as a flex option; the level 26 requirement makes it usable almost anywhere.
hold.risk: No scarcity premium, so holding has no real upside beyond convenience.
text: Worth keeping one low-penalty copy as a swap piece for freeze-heavy or dangerous-content farming.
Not an investment item; do not bank multiples expecting price growth.

entries.question: With Kitoko's Current equipped, does EVERY lightning hit build Electrocution, or only some of them?
summary: A player was unsure whether the glove makes all lightning damage contribute to Electrocution or only certain skills.
editorialAnalysis: The mod says 'Lightning damage from Hits Contributes to Electrocution Buildup'. It is global: any lightning damage your character deals as a Hit contributes, regardless of which skill produced it. It is not limited to one socketed skill the way the Electrocute Support Gem is.
officialAnswer: Yes - every lightning Hit your character lands contributes to Electrocution Buildup while the glove is equipped. Only Hits count; Damage over Time does not.

entries.question: The 15% reduced Attack and Cast Speed feels terrible. Can I just stack increased speed to cancel it out?
summary: A player wanted to negate the speed penalty with increased-Attack-and-Cast-Speed bonuses from gear and the tree.
editorialAnalysis: The penalty is 'reduced' (applied to your base speed), while increased-speed modifiers are added on top. So increased speed partly offsets the penalty but never removes it entirely. A 10% roll is much easier to cover than a 15% roll.
officialAnswer: You can soften the penalty with increased speed, but you cannot delete it. Pick a low (10%) roll or invest in speed if the loss bothers you.

entries.question: My Ignite build procs Kitoko's Current, right? Fire damage builds Electrocution too?
summary: A player assumed any damage-over-time would fill the Electrocution meter through the glove.
editorialAnalysis: The mod explicitly says 'from Hits'. Ignite, Poison, Bleed and other Damage over Time does not contribute to Electrocution Buildup through this item. You need actual lightning Hit damage.
officialAnswer: No. Only lightning damage from Hits counts. DoT-only setups gain nothing from the signature mod and still pay the speed penalty.

entries.question: Why does Kitoko's Current feel useless against the boss but great in maps?
summary: A player noticed reliable locks on packs but almost none on a pinnacle boss.
editorialAnalysis: Electrocution Buildup is mitigated by the enemy's Elemental Ailment Threshold, which scales with maximum life. A boss has far more life than a white mob, so the same Hit damage fills a much smaller fraction of the meter. Low-frequency, high-damage hits make this worse.
officialAnswer: Bosses have high thresholds. Sustain hit frequency or invest in ailment magnitude for boss control, or swap to Rare Gloves when control is not the bottleneck.

problems.symptom: Enemies are not getting stunned at all
directAnswer: Confirm you are dealing lightning damage as Hits (not DoT), and that the glove is actually equipped. Also remember bosses have a high threshold, so locks are slow, not absent.
checks: Verify the glove is in the active glove slot, not stored.
Check that your skill deals lightning Hit damage, not converted or Damage-over-Time.
On bosses, increase hit frequency or ailment magnitude.

problems.symptom: Cast speed feels too slow after equipping
directAnswer: That is the reduced Attack and Cast Speed roll. It cannot be fully removed, only offset by increased speed. A 15% roll hurts casters most.
checks: Check your roll (10% is far better than 15% for casters).
Add increased Cast Speed from gear, supports or the passive tree.
If still bad, swap to a Rare Glove.

directAnswer: The glove redirects lightning Hit buildup toward Electrocution, not toward bigger Shock. Your Hits still Shock normally, but the glove is a control item, not a damage multiplier.
checks: Treat the item as crowd control.
Keep Shock from your other lightning damage as usual.

directAnswer: By design. Only Hits contribute; Ignite/Poison/Bleed do nothing for the signature mod, and you still pay the speed penalty.
checks: Switch to a Rare Glove with real stats.
If you want Electrocution on a DoT build, use a different enabler, not this glove.

sections.title: Patch history and current vs legacy

changes: Kitoko's Current drops from the general unique pool with its current mod line: (30-50)% increased Energy Shield, +(10-20) Dexterity, (10-15)% reduced Attack and Cast Speed, and Lightning damage from Hits Contributes to Electrocution Buildup.
Electrocution is a current-gen ailment; the glove's redirect is valid against the live ailment threshold system.
The item has been in the game since 0.1.0 with the same core mod line; there is no older 'different' version that changed the Electrocution redirect or the speed-penalty range.

Because the only variable rolls are Energy Shield, Dexterity and the 10-15% speed penalty, 'legacy' here mainly means an older dropped roll range, not a functionally different item. A Divine Orb re-rolls the existing ranges; it cannot add or remove the Electrocution mod.
Kitoko's Current introduced to the game.
